classification.difficultyReason: Connect an odd factor count to the single equal-factor pair of a square, then generalise that connection to locate the next and largest eligible squares.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Explain why 25 has an odd number of factors.

answer.short: Its factors are $1, 5, 25$: three factors. The pair $5\times5$ contributes only one distinct factor.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}25&=1\times25\\25&=5\times5\end{align*}$$

The factors are $1,5,25$. The equal factors in $5\times5$ are counted once, giving three factors, an odd number.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the next whole number to have an odd number of factors?

answer.short:
$36$.

The next square number after $25$ is $6\times6=36$.
answer.worked:
Factors normally occur in distinct pairs. A square number has one equal-factor pair, so it has an odd number of factors.

The next square after $5\times5=25$ is $6\times6=36$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: What is the largest two-digit number with an odd number of factors?

answer.short:
$81$.

It is the largest two-digit square number.
answer.worked:
A number has an odd number of factors when it is a square number.

$9\times9=81$, whereas $10\times10=100$ has three digits. Therefore the largest two-digit number with an odd number of factors is $81$.
